study type: Secondary analysis for prediction model development
exposure: number of years since prior cesarean delivery (CD)
outcome: maternal complications (uterine dehiscence, hysterectomy, postpartum hemorrhage, endometritis, intensive care unit admission, thromboembolic event, readmission, organ injury)
neonatal complications (hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, respiratory distress, seizures, apnea, respirator use, death, cord blood pH < 7.1)
cohort: The study included 8,078 patients with term, singleton, cephalic presentation pregnancies who had one prior low transverse cesarean delivery and were considering a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC).
finding: A novel calculator was successfully developed and validated using modern mathematical techniques to predict both the likelihood of successful VBAC and the personalized risks of uterine rupture, composite maternal morbidity, and neonatal morbidity for patients considering TOLAC.
mod_finding: The advanced calculator provides comprehensive information to facilitate shared decision-making regarding the mode of birth by predicting the personalized risks and benefits associated with a trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC).
